title: Representative-normalized affine algebra-class comparison data
statement: For each commutative ring $B$, write $D(B)$ for its module derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $D(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B})$ for the sheaf derived category [def-pc-derived-category]. An affine realization comparison system consists of functors $F_B:D(B)\to D(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B})$ equipped with natural factorizations $QF_B\cong\widetilde{(-)}Q$ of the termwise associated-sheaf construction [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], natural tensor isomorphisms $\alpha_{P,Q}:F_BP\otimes^LF_BQ\cong F_B(P\otimes^LQ)$, and affine-open restriction isomorphisms $\rho_\varphi:j^*F_B\cong F_D L_\varphi$, where $L_\varphi=D\otimes_B^L-$ is the normalized ordinary derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Tensor and restriction identifications are fixed on K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex]: the total-tensor comparison restricts on each degree summand to the ordinary pure-tensor tilde map [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-tensor]; its derived tensor square uses the localization tensor map. The ordinary pullback comparison is the unit-normalized tilde/pullback map [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change], and its derived square uses the original recorded pullback counit [lem-pc-recorded-pullback-composition]. Require compatibility of $\rho$ with tensors using a normalized monoidal pullback model [def-pc-derived-pullback-monoidal-model]. Include composition isomorphisms $L_{\psi\varphi}\cong L_\psi L_\varphi$, normalized by the scalar-extension counits and the ordinary tensor associator, and require the successive-$\rho$ square using the recorded pullback composition. For such a system define $\gamma_{E,T}:F_B R\operatorname{Hom}_B(E,T)\to R\mathcal Hom(F_BE,F_BT)$ as the transpose of $\alpha;F_B(\mathrm{ev})$, using the recorded derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the representative-normalized sheaf tensor-Hom bijection [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection]. Define $\lambda_\varphi:L_\varphi R\operatorname{Hom}_B(E,T)\to R\operatorname{Hom}_D(L_\varphi E,L_\varphi T)$ by transposing extended evaluation. Define the open-Hom comparison by transposing pulled-back evaluation. For a commutative $B$-algebra $C$, put $E=C[0]$ and construct $\mu_C:E\otimes^LE\to E$ from ordinary multiplication and the localization tensor map, and multiplication by $c\in C$ by localizing its degree-zero linear map. For any multiplication $\mu:E\otimes^LE\to E$ and class $\xi:E\to T$, define $m_\xi$ as the module transpose of $\mu;\xi$, and define its sheaf counterpart for $E=C[0]$ by transposing the actual multiplication of the sheaf algebra $\widetilde C$ followed by the realized class. Construct this sheaf multiplication independently of the realization system: its ordinary degree-zero product is the inverse of the unique pure-tensor tilde isomorphism followed by $\widetilde{\operatorname{mul}_C}$; pass to the derived category using the localization tensor map. Identify $F_B(C[0])$ with $\widetilde C[0]$ through the recorded factorization and the single-complex comparison, and transport this sheaf product along that identification. Finally define $L_\varphi M[0]\to(D\otimes_B M)[0]$ using the scalar-extension counit and the ordinary single-complex comparison, and define the ordinary multiplication of $(D\otimes_B C)[0]$. These definitions assert no invertibility of $\gamma$, $\lambda$, or the degree-zero scalar-extension arrow.
